findings.reason: a node told to widen `normalise_unit` passes its own test while the `surfABVxp` fetch still aborts, so the boundary-RMS < 0.10 m check has no boundary contour (the sixteen frozen shots cache none) and the section's guard cannot fire; the plan must name `_unit` inside `REMOTE_SCRIPT` as the refusal on the fetch path.
findings.text: the paragraph says "`eddb_remote.normalise_unit` … refuses any multi-entry list, so a batch holding one aborts before it writes a channel. … the reader node changes `normalise_unit` to accept a multi-entry list whose entries all agree", but `normalise_unit` (`packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/eddb_remote.py:157-172`) is the *client-side decode* guard: `decode_batch` calls it on the header entry (`entry.get("unit", "")`, line 294), and the header's unit is written as a `str` by both `encode_batch` (`ChannelRecord.unit: str`) and the remote script (`"unit": record["unit"]`). The fetch path is `fetch_channels` → `RemoteEddbExtractor.fetch_batch` → the transport runs `REMOTE_SCRIPT`, and the refusal is the script's own `_unit` copy (`eddb_remote.py:437-446`), which reads the raw EDDB unit (`rtn.get("unit") or rtn.get("units")`) and raises a plain `RuntimeError` on a multi-entry list, crashing the script and aborting the batch. Reproduced at the worktree HEAD: `normalise_unit(["mm"]*3)` raises `EddbRemoteError`; `exec(REMOTE_SCRIPT)["_unit"](["mm"]*3)` raises `RuntimeError`; a `encode_batch`/`decode_batch` round-trip yields a `str` unit, so the client guard's list branch is unreachable on this path
